title: Coral and the Spire
premise: Cyrus Eastwick has spent six years hiding in the ledgers of the Meridian Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies, she learns the guild's founding covenant between the human city and the drowned realm beneath it is failing, and that a prophecy names an 'unseen scribe' as the one who must reforge it. Hunted by the guildmaster who wants the covenant broken and pursued by envoys of the drowning court who want her dead, Cyrus discovers her hedge-witch training in invisibility was itself a covenant-mark. In the spire at the city's heart, she must choose between restoring the old bargain—which demands a life—and writing a new one with her own blood and ink, ending the guild's monopoly on miracles even as it costs her the anonymity she built her life on.
about_author: Ulyana Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from port cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She balances the guild's books by candlelight: a bottled monsoon sold to a drought province, three years of memory pawned by a grieving widow. Establishes her careful invisibility and quiet pride in her work. Emotional beat: belonging found in numbers and order, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Date Written A Century Ago
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cataloguing the guildmaster's private collection, she opens a prophecy book sealed since the founding and finds tonight's date circled beside the words 'the unseen scribe.' The ink is still wet. Emotional beat: vertigo—the safe life revealed as a cage someone else designed.

chapters.title: What the Guildmaster Keeps Below
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, brief interlude from the guildmaster Vess. She descends into the guild vaults seeking answers and finds the original covenant: a treaty between the city and the drowned realm, its final clause torn out. Vess watches her, saying nothing. Emotional beat: dread blooming into resolve.

chapters.title: The Drowned Envoy
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An envoy from the realm beneath the harbor surfaces through the guild's well, expecting the covenant renewed; finding it broken, he marks Cyrus for death when she cannot produce the signatory. She flees using her hedge-witch vanishing arts—and realizes they are covenant-marks, not tricks. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV with flashback. She returns to her vanished mentor's cottage, now ransacked, and recovers letters revealing her teacher knew the prophecy and hid Cyrus inside the guild deliberately. Emotional beat: grief for the mentor reframed as inheritance—she was chosen, not abandoned.

chapters.title: Ink and Salt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Cyrus and Tam, a dockside smuggler who once sold the guild a stolen tide. He becomes her reluctant ally, ferrying her toward the spire while guild hunters close in. They bargain honestly with each other—a contrast to the guild's exploitative trades. Emotional beat: trust cautiously extended.

chapters.title: The Price of Miracles
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Captured by Vess, Tam learns the guildmaster engineered the covenant's collapse to monopolize the impossible, and that renewal requires a willing life given freely. Vess offers Tam freedom in exchange for betraying Cyrus's route. Emotional beat: temptation, and the corruption of institutionalized power laid bare.

chapters.title: The Spire Ascending
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Betrayed but alive—Tam gave false directions—she climbs the spire as the drowned realm rises against the harbor, water climbing the streets below. Vess intercepts her at the covenant chamber, offering partnership: keep the guild, share the power. Emotional beat: the seduction of power meeting hard-won integrity.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Refusing Vess, Cyrus invokes the torn clause's true terms: the covenant binds not a sacrifice but a witness—one who sees both realms and records them fairly. She signs in her own blood, naming the drowned and the city alike, and the flood recedes as the pact takes hold. Vess falls with the guild's authority. Emotional beat: justice written outside the law, at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, coda months later. The guild is dissolved into a public registry anyone may read or petition; Cyrus serves as its first neutral scribe, no longer invisible but no longer alone. Tam keeps the docks honest; the envoy returns with gifts, not threats. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not hidden—quiet, hard-won peace.
